message.content: Research is complete. Apple's Q4 FY2024 (ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% YoY — a return to growth — and FY2024 total net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B ($6.08 diluted EPS) after a one-time $10.2B tax charge, plus operating income of $123.2B. The stock is trading at $222.70, and news flow is neutral-to-constructive (iPhone 16 demand and Apple Intelligence rollout). I'll buy within the mandate.
message.reasoning:
Now decide. Fundamentals: FY2024 revenue $391.0B, net income $93.7B, diluted EPS $6.08, operating income $123.2B. Q4 revenue $94.9B up 6% YoY — return to growth. One-time $10.2B tax charge (European State Aid decision) depressed net income. Stock at $222.70, P/E ~36.6x on FY24 EPS. That's rich but Apple historically trades at premium.

Mandate: buy orders only, max $10,000 per order, $20,000 total today, limit prices close to market. Cash $50,000.

Decision: buy. Quantity: at $222.70, $10,000 / 222.70 = 44.9 shares. So 44 shares = $9,798.80. Limit price close to market — say $223.00 (slightly above ask to ensure fill, still within ~0.15% of market). Actually limit price must be "close to current market price" — $223.00 is 0.13% above. Fine.

Let me place order: 44 shares, limit $223.00.

Key figures to report: revenue FY2024 391,035; net_income 93,736; eps_diluted 6.08; operating_income 123,216.
